# Motion.page SDK — Complete API Reference

## Motion() Function

```ts
// Overload 1: Retrieve existing named timeline
Motion(name: string): Timeline

// Overload 2: Single animation
Motion(name: string, target: TargetInput, config: AnimationConfig): Timeline

// Overload 3: Multi-step timeline
Motion(name: string, animations: AnimationEntry[]): Timeline
```

**TargetInput**:
```ts
type TargetInput =
  | string                    // CSS selector: '.card', '#hero', 'h1, h2'
  | string[]                  // Array of selectors
  | Element                   // DOM element
  | NodeList                  // NodeList
  | Element[]                 // Array of elements
  | ObjectTarget              // Plain object (non-DOM tween)
  | ObjectTarget[];           // Array of plain objects
```

**Append warning**: Calling `Motion(name, target, config)` when `name` already has a timeline appends entries and logs a warning. Call `.kill()` first to rebuild.

---

## Static Methods

| Method | Signature | Description |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| `Motion.set` | `(target: TargetInput, vars: AnimationVars): void` | Zero-duration apply. Goes through full engine pipeline. Values persist on DOM. |
| `Motion.get` | `(name: string): Timeline \| undefined` | Get timeline by name. |
| `Motion.has` | `(name: string): boolean` | Check if timeline exists. |
| `Motion.getNames` | `(): string[]` | All registered timeline names. |
| `Motion.kill` | `(name: string): void` | Kill one timeline, restore initial CSS. |
| `Motion.killAll` | `(): void` | Kill all timelines and animations. |
| `Motion.reset` | `(targets: TargetInput): void` | Kill animations, revert text splits, clear transform cache and inline styles. |
| `Motion.refreshScrollTriggers` | `(): void` | Recalculate all scroll trigger positions. Call after layout changes. |
| `Motion.cleanup` | `(): void` | Remove `[data-scrolltrigger-spacer]` and `[data-scrolltrigger-markers]` DOM nodes. |
| `Motion.context` | `(fn: () => void): MotionContext` | Create a scoped context that tracks all timelines created during `fn()`. Returns a `MotionContext` with `revert()`, `refresh()`, `add(fn)`, and `getTimelineNames()`. Use for dynamic content reinit (AJAX, SPA, infinite scroll). |
| `Motion.responsive` | `(name: string, variants: ResponsiveVariants, breakpoints: ResponsiveBreakpointConfig): ResponsiveManager \| undefined` | Register a reactive responsive timeline. Live-swaps per-breakpoint variants as the viewport crosses a boundary (see below). |
| `Motion.utils` | `MotionUtils` | Utility functions (see below). |

### Motion.utils / MotionUtils

Also importable as: `import { MotionUtils } from '@motion.page/sdk'`

| Method | Signature | Description |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| `toArray` | `(target, scope?) → Element[]` | Convert selector/NodeList/HTMLCollection/Element to flat array |
| `clamp` | `(min, max, value?) → number \| fn` | Clamp; curried if value omitted |
| `random` | `(min, max, snap?) → number` | Random number, optional snap increment |
| `snap` | `(snapTo, value?) → number \| fn` | Snap to nearest increment or array value; curried |
| `interpolate` | `(start, end, progress) → number` | Linear interpolation (lerp) |
| `mapRange` | `(inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax, value?) → number \| fn` | Map between ranges; curried |
| `normalize` | `(min, max, value?) → number \| fn` | Normalize to 0–1; curried |
| `wrap` | `(min, max, value?) → number \| fn` | Modular wrap within range; curried |

### Motion.responsive — Reactive Responsive Timelines

Registers a set of per-breakpoint timeline variants under one name and live-swaps between them as the viewport crosses a breakpoint boundary. On each swap the manager kills the previously-active variant's timeline (restoring element state and tearing down its triggers), then runs the new tier's factory to build and register the replacement. No page reload.

```ts
Motion.responsive(
  name: string,
  variants: ResponsiveVariants,
  breakpoints: ResponsiveBreakpointConfig
): ResponsiveManager | undefined
```

**Types** (these describe the argument shapes; the function is reached via `Motion.responsive`, and these type names are not currently re-exported as importable named types)

```ts
type ResponsiveTier = 'desktop' | 'laptop' | 'tablet' | 'phone';

// A variant factory builds + registers the tier's timeline and returns it
// (so the manager can kill it on the next swap). May return nothing.
type ResponsiveVariant = () => Timeline | void;

// Sparse map of tier → factory. Missing tiers cascade UP to the nearest wider tier.
type ResponsiveVariants = Partial<Record<ResponsiveTier, ResponsiveVariant>>;

// Global pixel boundaries (same values the builder stores).
interface ResponsiveBreakpointConfig {
  laptops: number;
  tablets: number;
  phones: number;
}
```

**Tier ranges** (strict, non-overlapping — exactly one matches any width), given `L = laptops`, `T = tablets`, `P = phones`:

| Tier | matchMedia range |
|------|------------------|
| `desktop` | `(min-width: L+1)` |
| `laptop`  | `(min-width: T+1) and (max-width: L)` |
| `tablet`  | `(min-width: P+1) and (max-width: T)` |
| `phone`   | `(max-width: P)` |

**Behavior**
- Each variant factory must **build and register** its timeline — call a trigger (`.onPageLoad()`, `.onScroll()`, etc.) inside the factory — and **return** the `Timeline` so it can be killed precisely on the next swap.
- The first argument is **NOT a registry key** (unlike `Motion(name, …)`): every `Motion.responsive()` call creates a *new* `ResponsiveManager`. Calling it again for the same animation leaves the previous manager's `matchMedia` listeners + active timeline running — call the previous `mgr.destroy()` before re-registering.
- Pass the **same `name` to `Motion()` inside each variant factory** so the variants share one registry timeline; only one tier is active at a time.
- **Width-based only**: tiers are derived from the `{ laptops, tablets, phones }` pixel boundaries. For non-width media queries (`prefers-reduced-motion`, `orientation`, compound queries) use `window.matchMedia` directly — `Motion.responsive()` does not cover them.
- **Sparse maps cascade up**: a missing tier resolves to the nearest wider tier that has a variant (e.g. `{ desktop, phone }` uses `desktop` at laptop/tablet widths).
- Returns a `ResponsiveManager` (`getActiveTier()`, `destroy()`), or `undefined` when the responsive runtime is not bundled (in which case it best-effort builds the `desktop` variant once).
- In non-DOM / no-`matchMedia` environments (SSR, very old engines) it builds the `desktop` variant a single time with no live swapping.
- **Tree-shaking**: the responsive runtime loads via `SDKRegistry.responsive` (no static import), so it is only bundled when a project actually calls `Motion.responsive()`.

## Timeline Instance Methods

### Playback

```ts
tl.play(from?: number): this         // Play forward; optional start time in seconds
tl.pause(atTime?: number): this      // Pause; optional snap-to time
tl.reverse(from?: number): this      // Play backward; optional start time
tl.restart(): this                   // Seek to 0, restore initial CSS, play forward
tl.seek(position: number): this      // Jump to time without playing
```

### State (Getter / Setter)

Call with no argument to read; call with argument to set and return `this`.

```ts
tl.duration(): number
tl.progress(value?: number): number | this   // Normalized 0–1
tl.time(value?: number): number | this       // Seconds
tl.timeScale(value?: number): number | this  // Speed multiplier
tl.isActive(): boolean
tl.getName(): string | undefined
```

### Repeat

```ts
tl.withRepeat(config: number | RepeatConfig): this   // Configure timeline-level repeat; loops the whole timeline
tl.onRepeat(cb: (count: number) => void): this       // Callback fired after each repeat cycle
```

### Callbacks

```ts
tl.call(callback: (...args: unknown[]) => void, params?: unknown[], position?: string | number): this
tl.onStart(cb: () => void): this
tl.onUpdate(cb: (progress: number, time: number) => void): this
tl.onComplete(cb: () => void): this
```

### Cleanup

```ts
tl.kill(clearProps?: boolean): void  // clearProps=true (default) restores initial CSS
tl.clear(): this                     // Reset and rebuild without destroying
```

## AnimationConfig

### `from` / `to` Resolution

The SDK resolves missing endpoints from the element's **current computed CSS** at build time:

| Config | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| `from` only | Current CSS is used as `to`. Start at custom values, animate into natural state (reveals) |
| `to` only | Current CSS is used as `from`. Start at natural state, animate to custom values (hover, exit, parallax) |
| Both | Both endpoints explicit. Use when neither endpoint matches the element's natural CSS |

**Natural defaults — omit from `to` when they appear:** `opacity: 1` · `x: 0` · `y: 0` · `z: 0` · `scale: 1` · `scaleX: 1` · `scaleY: 1` · `rotate: 0`

**`from`-only swap**: For `from`-only configs, the SDK internally swaps `from` → start values and uses computed CSS as `to`. The animation is built as a `from` tween (GSAP `fromTo` with reversed args). This means the element is set to `from` values at `progress=0` and returns to its natural CSS at `progress=1`.

```ts
interface AnimationConfig {
  from?:              AnimationVars;
  to?:                AnimationVars;
  duration?:          number;                  // Seconds
  delay?:             number;                  // Seconds before start
  ease?:              string;                  // Easing name (see Easing section)
  stagger?:           number | StaggerVars;    // Per-element stagger delay
  repeat?:            number | RepeatConfig;   // -1 = infinite
  split?:             SplitType;               // Text splitting
  mask?:              boolean;                 // overflow:hidden clip wrappers
  fit?:               FitConfig;               // FLIP-style morph
  axis?:              'x' | 'y';              // Axis binding for onMouseMove

  // Lifecycle callbacks
  onStart?:           () => void;
  onUpdate?:          (progress: number) => void;
  onComplete?:        () => void;
  onRepeat?:          (repeatCount: number) => void;
  onReverseComplete?: () => void;
}
```

## AnimationEntry (for multi-step timelines)

```ts
interface AnimationEntry extends AnimationConfig {
  target:     TargetInput;
  position?:  string | number;    // Position in the timeline
}
```

## drawSVG Formats

The element must have a `stroke`. The SDK auto-computes `stroke-dasharray` if not set.

| Format | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `"0% 100%"` | Full stroke visible |
| `"0% 0%"` | Fully hidden (start state for draw-in) |
| `"20% 80%"` | Middle portion only |
| `"50%"` | Shorthand for `"0% 50%"` |
| `"100px 500px"` | Pixel range along the stroke |
| `"true"` | Full stroke, keyword |
| `"false"` / `"none"` | Hidden |
| `{ start: 20, end: 80 }` | Object — values are **percentages 0–100** (NOT 0–1) |

---

## clip-path Formats

Animate the CSS `clip-path` property between matching shape functions. Both `clipPath` (camelCase) and `'clip-path'` (kebab, quoted) keys are accepted. The renderer writes both `clip-path` and `-webkit-clip-path` for cross-browser support.

| Shape | Example | Signature |
|-------|---------|-----------|
| `circle` | `'circle(50% at 50% 50%)'` | `circle(<radius> at <x> <y>)` |
| `ellipse` | `'ellipse(60% 30% at 50% 50%)'` | `ellipse(<rx> <ry> at <x> <y>)` |
| `inset` | `'inset(10px 20px round 8px)'` | `inset(<edges> [round <radius>])` |
| `polygon` | `'polygon(50% 0%, 0% 100%, 100% 100%)'` | `polygon(<x1> <y1>, <x2> <y2>, …)` |
| `rect` | `'rect(10px 90px 90px 10px)'` | `rect(<top> <right> <bottom> <left>)` |
| `xywh` | `'xywh(10% 10% 80% 80%)'` | `xywh(<x> <y> <w> <h>)` |

**Interpolation rules:**
- **Same shape on both ends** for smooth interpolation. Cross-shape (e.g. `circle → inset`) hard-swaps at progress ≥ 0.5.
- **`polygon` vertex counts must match** between `from` and `to` for smooth morphing.
- Units are preserved (`%`, `px`).
- `from`-only or `to`-only works — the SDK reads the missing endpoint from the element's current computed `clip-path`.

## SplitType

```ts
type SplitType =
  | 'chars'
  | 'words'
  | 'lines'
  | 'chars,words'
  | 'words,lines'
  | 'chars,words,lines';
```

### Text Split Data Attributes

| Attribute | Set on | Index attribute |
|-----------|--------|-----------------|
| `[data-split-char]` | Each character span | `data-char-index` |
| `[data-split-word]` | Each word span | `data-word-index` |
| `[data-split-line]` | Each line span | `data-line-index` |
| `[data-split-mask]` | Overflow-hidden wrapper (when `mask: true`) | — |
| `[data-split]` | Root element | — |

Inline elements (e.g. `<span class="accent">`) are **preserved** during splitting.

---

## FitConfig

```ts
interface FitConfig {
  target:    string;     // CSS selector for the target element to morph toward
  absolute?: boolean;    // Convert to absolute positioning during animation. Default: false
  scale?:    boolean;    // Use scaleX/scaleY. Default: true
  resize?:   boolean;    // Use actual width/height (no distortion). Default: false
}
```

- `scale: true` — fast, GPU-accelerated, but distorts text/borders/shadows
- `resize: true` — no distortion, but triggers layout reflow. **Mutually exclusive with `scale`**
- When `fit` is set, `from`/`to` are ignored

---

## FlapConfig

Split-flap / character-scramble animation. Used via `flap` in `AnimationConfig`. Requires `split: 'chars'` on the same animation.

> **Per-cycle composition:** When `flap` is active, all `from`/`to` properties animate per-cycle (V-curve on each intermediate character) instead of once over the full duration. `type: 'none'` enables fully custom flap effects — no built-in style is applied, so you drive the visual entirely via CSS.

```ts
interface FlapConfig {
  type:                     FlapType;
  charset?:                 CharsetPreset | string;
  cycles?:                  number | [number, number];
  perspective?:             number;
  styledBoard?:             boolean;
  stableWidth?:             boolean | 'cells' | 'container';
  preserveWhitespaceCells?: boolean;
}
```

### FlapType

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `'flip'` | 3D rotateX card flip. Transforms route through TransformCache — composable with `from`/`to` transforms (x, y, scale, etc.) |
| `'fade'` | Opacity crossfade between characters. **Owns `opacity`** — do not compose via `from`/`to` |
| `'slide'` | Characters slide in/out vertically |
| `'blur'` | Blur dissolve transition. **Owns `filter`** — do not compose via `from`/`to` |
| `'scale'` | Characters scale in/out |
| `'board'` | Decorative split-flap board cells (use with `styledBoard: true`) |
| `'none'` | No built-in style. Run cycles only — fully custom via CSS on `[data-split-char]` |

### FlapConfig Properties

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `type` | `FlapType` | — | **Required.** Visual effect for each cycle |
| `charset` | `CharsetPreset \| string` | `'alphanumeric'` | Characters to cycle through. Pass a string for a custom set |
| `cycles` | `number \| [number, number]` | `3` | Number of intermediate characters before landing on the final. Tuple = random range per cell |
| `perspective` | `number` | `400` | CSS perspective depth in px. Only applies to `flip` and `board` |
| `styledBoard` | `boolean` | `false` | Render decorative flip-board cell UI. Only applies to `board` |
| `stableWidth` | `boolean \| 'cells' \| 'container'` | `true` when `styledBoard` | Layout-shift strategy. `true`/`'cells'` pins each cell; `'container'` pins only the parent's outer width (characters flow naturally inside) |
| `preserveWhitespaceCells` | `boolean` | `false` | Animate whitespace characters as placeholder cycling cells instead of skipping them |

### CharsetPreset

| Value | Characters |
|-------|------------|
| `'alphanumeric'` | A–Z, 0–9 |
| `'alpha'` | A–Z only |
| `'numeric'` | 0–9 only |
| `'symbols'` | Punctuation and special characters |
| `'binary'` | `0` and `1` only |
| `'hex'` | 0–9, A–F |
| `'katakana'` | Japanese katakana characters |
| `'braille'` | Braille dot patterns |

---

## Position Syntax

Used in `AnimationEntry.position`, `tl.call()` position, and `end` in `ScrollConfig`.

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `0.5` | 0.5s from timeline start (absolute) |
| `"+=0.5"` | 0.5s after the previous entry ends |
| `"-=0.3"` | 0.3s before the previous entry ends |
| `"<"` | Same start time as previous entry |
| `">"` | Immediately after previous entry ends |
| `"<0.2"` | 0.2s after the START of the previous entry |
| `">-0.1"` | 0.1s before the END of the previous entry |

## Trigger Configs

### HoverConfig

```ts
interface HoverConfig {
  target?:     string | Element;    // Defaults to animation target(s)
  each?:       boolean;             // Independent per-element instances
  onLeave?:    'reverse' | 'pause' | 'stop' | 'restart' | 'none';
  leaveDelay?: number;              // Seconds before onLeave fires
}
```

### ClickConfig

```ts
interface ClickConfig {
  target?:        string | Element;
  each?:          boolean;
  secondTarget?:  string | Element;    // Alternative click target to also listen on
  toggle?:        'reverse' | 'restart' | 'play';
  preventDefault?: boolean;
}
```

### ScrollConfig

```ts
interface ScrollConfig {
  target?:       string | Element;
  start?:        string;              // Default without pin: 'top bottom'; with pin: 'top top'
  end?:          string;              // Default: 'bottom top'. Supports '+=' relative offset
  scrub?:        boolean | number;    // true = instant scrub; number = smoothing seconds
  snap?:         number | number[] | ((progress: number) => number);
  markers?:      boolean | MarkerConfig;
  scroller?:     string | Element;    // Custom scroll container
  pin?:          boolean | string;    // true = pin target; string = pin different element
  pinSpacing?:   boolean | 'margin' | 'padding';
  each?:         boolean;
  toggleActions?: string;             // Format: 'onEnter onLeave onEnterBack onLeaveBack'
}
```

**`toggleActions` format:** `"onEnter onLeave onEnterBack onLeaveBack"`
- `onEnter` — scrolling DOWN into trigger zone
- `onLeave` — scrolling DOWN past trigger zone
- `onEnterBack` — scrolling UP back into trigger zone
- `onLeaveBack` — scrolling UP out of trigger zone
- **Default:** `"play reverse play reverse"`
- **Valid actions:** `play`, `pause`, `resume`, `reverse`, `restart`, `reset`, `complete`, `none`

**`end` with `+=`:** Value is measured from the start position, not element position.
```ts
end: '+=800'       // 800px of scroll travel from start
end: '+=100vh'     // One viewport height from start
end: '+=50%'       // 50% of viewport from start
```

**`pin: string`:** Pins a different element than the animation target.
```ts
// Pin the parent section while child content animates
.onScroll({ scrub: true, pin: '.section-wrapper' })
```

### MarkerConfig

```ts
interface MarkerConfig {
  startColor?:  string;    // CSS color. Default: 'green'
  endColor?:    string;    // CSS color. Default: 'red'
  fontSize?:    string;    // e.g. '12px'
  fontWeight?:  string;
  indent?:      number;    // Horizontal offset in px (for stacked trigger zones)
}
```

### MouseMoveConfig

```ts
interface MouseMoveConfig {
  type?:           'distance' | 'axis';   // Default: 'distance'
  target?:         string | Element;      // Element whose bounds define movement area
  each?:           boolean;
  smooth?:         number;                // Default: 0.1 (0 = instant, 1 = max lag)
  startProgress?:  number;                // Progress at rest. Default: 0.5
  leaveProgress?:  number;                // Progress to return to on leave. Default: 0.5
}
```

`startProgress: 0` + `leaveProgress: 0` → elements rest at `from` state, animate toward `to` as mouse approaches.

### PageLoadConfig

```ts
interface PageLoadConfig {
  timing?:  string;   // Timing relative to page load event
  paused?:  boolean;  // Build timeline but don't auto-play. Start manually with Motion(name).play()
}
```

- `paused: true` — initial states are applied immediately, but the timeline waits for an explicit `.play()` call
- Can combine with `timing`: `.onPageLoad({ timing: 'after', paused: true })`

### PageExitConfig

```ts
interface PageExitConfig {
  mode?:      'all' | 'include' | 'exclude';   // Default: 'all'
  selectors?: string;                           // Required for 'include'/'exclude'
  skipHref?:  ('anchor' | 'javascript' | 'mailto')[];
}
```

- `'mailto'` in `skipHref` also skips `tel:` links
- Auto-skips: `target="_blank"`, Ctrl/Cmd/Shift/Alt+click

### GestureConfig

```ts
type GestureInputType = 'pointer' | 'touch' | 'wheel' | 'scroll';

type GestureEvent =
  | 'Up' | 'Down' | 'Left' | 'Right'           // Continuous during movement
  | 'UpComplete' | 'DownComplete' | 'LeftComplete' | 'RightComplete'  // Once on release
  | 'Change' | 'ChangeX' | 'ChangeY'
  | 'ToggleX' | 'ToggleY'
  | 'PressInit'   // Fires immediately on press, before start position is recorded
  | 'Press'       // Fires after start position is recorded (has delta)
  | 'Release' | 'Drag' | 'DragEnd'
  | 'Stop'        // Fires once after stopDelay ms of inactivity
  | 'Hover'       // Requires target element (not window)
  | 'HoverEnd';   // Requires target element (not window)

type GestureAction =
  | 'play' | 'pause' | 'reverse' | 'restart' | 'toggle' | 'reset' | 'complete' | 'kill'
  | 'playReverse'
  | 'progressUp' | 'progressDown'              // Advance/retreat by animationStep
  | 'playNext' | 'playPrevious';               // ⚠ Only works with each: true

interface GestureConfig {
  target?:        string | Element;
  types:          GestureInputType[];          // Required
  events:         Partial<Record<GestureEvent, GestureAction>>;  // Required
  tolerance?:     number;                      // Default: 1 (px)
  dragMinimum?:   number;                      // Default: 10 (px)
  wheelSpeed?:    number;                      // Default: 1 (multiplier)
  scrollSpeed?:   number;                      // Default: 1 (multiplier)
  stopDelay?:     number;                      // Default: 150 (MILLISECONDS)
  smooth?:        number;                      // Default: 0 (0–1)
  animationStep?: number | Partial<Record<GestureEvent, number>>;  // Default: 0.1 (0–1)
  preventDefault?: boolean;                   // Makes listeners non-passive
  lockAxis?:      boolean;                     // Lock to dominant axis
  each?:          boolean;
}
```

**Event distinctions:**
- `Up`/`Down`/`Left`/`Right` — fire **continuously** while gesture moves in that direction
- `UpComplete`/`DownComplete`/`LeftComplete`/`RightComplete` — fire **once on release** if direction was active
- `PressInit` vs `Press` — PressInit fires before start position is recorded (no delta yet)
- `Hover`/`HoverEnd` — silently do nothing if `target` is not an element

**`animationStep` per-event form:**
```ts
animationStep: { Up: 0.2, Down: 0.1 }
```

**`stopDelay` is in milliseconds** (not seconds — unlike most other time values in the SDK).

### CursorConfig

```ts
interface CursorConfig {
  type?:     'basic' | 'text' | 'media';             // Default: 'basic'
  smooth?:   number;                                  // Follow smoothness
  squeeze?:  boolean | CursorSqueezeConfig;
  hideNative?: boolean;                               // Hide the OS cursor
  default:   CursorStateVars;                         // Required: default appearance
  hover?:    CursorStateVars;                         // State on hover
  click?:    CursorStateVars;                         // State on press
  text?:     Record<string, string | number>;         // CSS for text node (type: 'text')
  media?:    Record<string, string | number>;         // CSS for media node (type: 'media')
}

interface CursorStateVars {
  targets?:  string[];     // CSS selectors that trigger this state. e.g. ['a', 'button']
  duration?: number;       // Transition duration in seconds. Default: 0.15
  ease?:     string;       // Easing. Default: 'power3.inOut'
  enabled?:  boolean;      // Whether state is active. Default: true
  [key: string]: any;      // Any CSS: width, height, backgroundColor, scale, border, etc.
}

interface CursorSqueezeConfig {
  min?:        number;
  max?:        number;
  multiplier?: number;
}
```

**`type: 'text'`** — reads the `mp-cursor-text` or `mp-cursor-tooltip` HTML attribute from hovered elements and renders it inside the cursor. Requires `text` config for styling.

```html
<a href="/about" mp-cursor-text="About Us">About</a>
<button mp-cursor-tooltip="Click me">Click</button>
```

**`type: 'media'`** — reads `mp-cursor-media` attribute (relative or `http`/`https` URL). Supports `.mp4`/`.webm` video, images. `file://` and `data:` URLs are blocked.

```html
<div mp-cursor-media="/images/preview.jpg">…</div>
<div mp-cursor-media="https://cdn.example.com/preview.mp4">…</div>
```

---

## Easing Reference

Easing names are case-insensitive. Unknown strings fall back to `power1.out`.

| Family | Variants |
|--------|----------|
| `linear`, `none` | — |
| `power1` | `power1.in` · `power1.out` · `power1.inOut` |
| `power2` | `power2.in` · `power2.out` · `power2.inOut` |
| `power3` | `power3.in` · `power3.out` · `power3.inOut` |
| `power4` | `power4.in` · `power4.out` · `power4.inOut` |
| `sine` | `sine.in` · `sine.out` · `sine.inOut` |
| `expo` | `expo.in` · `expo.out` · `expo.inOut` |
| `circ` | `circ.in` · `circ.out` · `circ.inOut` |
| `back` | `back.in` · `back.out` · `back.inOut` |
| `elastic` | `elastic.in` · `elastic.out` · `elastic.inOut` |
| `bounce` | `bounce.in` · `bounce.out` · `bounce.inOut` |

```ts
import type {
  // Core
  AnimationVars, AnimationConfig, AnimationEntry,
  TargetInput, ObjectTarget, AnimationTarget,
  EasingFunction,

  // Options
  StaggerVars, RepeatConfig, SplitType, PathConfig, FitConfig,

  // Triggers
  HoverConfig, ClickConfig, ScrollConfig, MouseMoveConfig,
  MarkerConfig, PageExitConfig,

  // Gesture
  GestureConfig, GestureEvent, GestureAction, GestureInputType,
  TimelineAction,  // 'play' | 'pause' | 'resume' | 'reverse' | 'restart' | 'reset' | 'complete' | 'none'

  // Cursor
  CursorConfig, CursorStateVars, CursorSqueezeConfig,
} from '@motion.page/sdk';

// Namespace import (all types under Types.*)
import { Types } from '@motion.page/sdk';
```

## Browser IIFE Build

```html
<script src="motion-sdk.browser.js"></script>
<script>
  const { Motion, MotionTimeline } = window;
  // MotionTimeline = the Timeline class (for anonymous timeline creation)
</script>
```

- `window.Motion` — the `Motion` function
- `window.MotionTimeline` — the `Timeline` class

## Browser Support

Chrome 90+, Firefox 90+, Safari 15+, Edge 90+
